summary: Crash when changing render distance / java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: Index 28084 out of bounds for length 26136
description: When changing render/view distance via the option menu while standing inside a world, minecraft sometimes crashes with an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. This can be best reproduced by spam-clicking the slider in random positions, although for me it crashed after only one click, the first time.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Create or load a Singleplayer world with default settings.
2. Enter the Options menu and navigate to Video Settings.
3. While standing inside the world, spam-click the Render Distance slider in random positions.
4. Observe that Minecraft sometimes crashes with an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException when changing render distance via the option menu.
5. Take note of any error messages or crash reports generated during the reproduction attempt.

6. If the bug does not occur immediately, repeat steps 2-4 multiple times to increase the likelihood of reproducing the issue.
Observed Behavior: When changing the render/view distance via the option menu while standing inside a world, Minecraft sometimes crashes with an `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`. This issue can be best reproduced by rapidly clicking the slider in random positions, although it has also been observed to occur after only one click. The error message indicates that the index 28084 is out of bounds for a length of 26136, suggesting a mismatch or overflow in array handling related to render distance adjustments. This bug affects gameplay by causing unexpected crashes when players attempt to modify their view settings.
Expected Behavior: When changing the render/view distance via the option menu while standing inside a world, Minecraft should not crash and should successfully update the render distance without any exceptions or errors. The game should remain stable regardless of how quickly or frequently the slider is adjusted.
